requiring both names and emails to be unique.

preserving identity matching for linked applications. Exclude the
applicant being edited when checking other records for conflicts.

or an empty panel, preventing users from reviewing what was removed.

document the deletion behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add applicant selection to command results
commitResults.messageBody:
Command results only carry feedback and help or exit actions, so the
UI cannot identify an applicant to select after a command succeeds.

Add an optional applicant selection to command results while preserving
the existing defaults. Cover the new result state in constructor,
equality, and hash code tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Connect view commands to applicant details
commitResults.messageBody:
The view command prints contact details without updating the selected
applicant, leaving the detail panel out of sync with the command.

Select and scroll to the requested applicant, and show a short
confirmation alongside the detail panel. Preserve filtered list indices
and failed-command selections, with regression coverage for both.

Fixes #68

The view guide describes name and email output in the command result
display, which no longer matches the applicant detail workflow.

Describe list selection, scrolling, and the details shown in the panel.
Include an example that selects an applicant from filtered results.

commitResults.messageBody:
The add command uses slash prefixes even though a shared tokenizer
supports hyphen options.

Use that tokenizer to accept short and long aliases for all four
required person fields and reject the legacy add syntax. Preserve field
validation and edit syntax, and update usage hints and test fixtures.

Cover aliases, malformed options, legacy input, and saving a person
through the logic layer.

commitResults.messageBody:

rules so users can construct valid add commands.

and recreating the role.

commitResults.messageBody:
An application-only deletion must survive a restart and free the

reload the saved records, and verify that addp can record a new
application while the existing job remains stored.

Deleting an application from a filtered list should select the affected
applicant and clear the old application details. Cover this workflow in
the UI while checking that the applicant filter remains unchanged.
